paths.description: Homepage listing: primary discovery template, preference/mobile/performance/security/memory target.
Myanmar category: representative taxonomy/listing archetype; confirms shared grid template.
Video detail: representative core playback journey, custom media controls, metadata, related content and third-party ad surface.
Deliberate missing URL: representative HTTP failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: The fixed dark palette does not participate in the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical in size and appearance to the default capture, while the preferences probe reports colorScheme "normal" and the CSS probe finds no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens, retaining the existing dark treatment as the dark branch.

findings.summary: Transitions and animations have no reduced-motion override.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found 11 transitions and 2 animations but no prefers-reduced-motion rule; the reduced-motion probe still observed a 1000 ms animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that removes non-essential transitions/animations and preserves only necessary state changes.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found no view-transition CSS and the MPA document contains no cross-document transition rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin category and detail navigation with @view-transition { navigation: auto }, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide no scroll-state feedback or return affordance.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout is 3,425 px tall, while the screenshots and CSS probe show static navigation with no progress indicator, shrinking header, scroll-state query, or equivalent position feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or position-aware return control, preferably declarative and reduced-motion safe.

findings.summary: The mobile menu trigger is an unlabelled, non-keyboard-operable div.
findings.evidence:
DOM inspection identifies
as the menu trigger; it is absent from the focusable-controls probe and exposes no name, role, expanded state, or controlled target.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real button with an accessible name, aria-expanded and aria-controls; preserve focus and make Escape/dismiss behavior predictable.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rule and 104 physical-direction declarations; the grid changes at the viewport level only.
findings.suggestedFix: Define container-type on reusable listing/player regions and use size container queries where the component layout, not the viewport, determines available space.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch targets are inadequate on primary controls.
findings.evidence: Focused links and player controls report outline style "none"; the menu trigger is not focusable, and seven player controls are 28×28 px, below a comfortable touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible :focus-visible styling, replace the menu div with a button, and expand player controls to at least 44×44 CSS px without shrinking the icon.

findings.summary: Throttled LCP is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.5 s (score 0.65), although the local trace measured 1.4 s; CLS was 0 and TBT was 3 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the first visible thumbnail/LCP candidate, reduce blocking font/style work, and verify field LCP after deployment.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking CSS and legacy scripts lengthen the critical path.
findings.evidence: The HAR summary identifies four VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets and parser-inserted jQuery/jquery-migrate scripts; Google Fonts also sits on the critical path.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline or consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, remove jquery-migrate if unused, and self-host/subset the one font actually needed.

findings.summary: Analytics is the largest script and ships substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports about 68 KiB of unused JavaScript in gtag; the HAR records gtag as the largest resource at 160,795 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics only after an appropriate consent/interaction point, or replace it with a smaller privacy-preserving measurement path.

findings.summary: Content thumbnails and custom player controls lack robust accessible names.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports all 12 homepage thumbnails without meaningful alt text and 10 missing on the detail page; several SVG-only player buttons have no aria-label or text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give linked thumbnails concise content-specific alt text (or name the image link), and add stable accessible names to every custom player button.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy and focus presentation are not accessible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags an H1-to-H3 heading-order skip; the detail page has two H1s, and focused elements report outline style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page H1, nest card headings sequentially, add main/header/footer landmarks consistently, and provide a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: User zoom is restricted, player controls are undersized, and the video has no captions track.
findings.evidence: The viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1; player controls are 28×28 px and the 473-second video exposes zero track elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale, enlarge targets, and provide a captions/subtitles track or an equivalent transcript for spoken content.

findings.summary: Detail-page assets are inconsistently sized and delivered.
findings.evidence: The detail images primitive reports 4 images without dimensions, 6 oversized images, 6 without responsive sources, and 5 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height, responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images, and remove hidden duplicate image requests.

findings.summary: Pages have titles but no meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: DOM and Lighthouse evidence show a descriptive title but no meta[name=description] on the home and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise, unique description for listing, category, and detail templates from visible page content.

findings.summary: The homepage omits a canonical URL.
findings.evidence: The homepage metadata probe reports canonical null; detail pages do expose a self-canonical and robots.txt points to a valid WordPress sitemap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a self-referencing canonical to the homepage and category templates while retaining the existing detail canonicals.

findings.summary: Video detail pages lack share-preview and structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The detail probe finds no Open Graph tags and no JSON-LD despite the page representing a named video with a poster and duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and VideoObject JSON-LD that matches the visible title, thumbnail, upload date, duration, and canonical URL.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers and cookie protections are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports missing CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; both analytics cookies are non-Secure, SameSite=None, and 400 days long.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark necessary cookies Secure with an appropriate SameSite value and shorter lifetime.

findings.summary: Tracking starts on load and persists for 400 days without an observed consent choice.
findings.evidence: The tracker primitive finds Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics across 5 third-party origins; two analytics cookies are created on load for 400 days, and third parties transfer 223,220 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not load non-essential analytics until an informed choice where required; shorten retention, minimize events, and document the data path.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: No CSP/frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy the missing policies at the origin, start CSP in report-only mode, then enforce a nonce/hash-based policy and explicit frame-ancestors.

findings.summary: The Burmese-language experience is declared as English and uses only physical CSS directions.
findings.evidence: Both listing and detail DOM report html lang="en-US" while the visible content is predominantly Burmese; the CSS probe finds 0 logical and 104 physical-direction declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Set the page language to my (or the precise locale), mark language changes, and migrate layout rules to logical inline/block properties.

findings.summary: Image delivery leaves avoidable byte and resolution waste.
findings.evidence: All 12 homepage thumbnails are JPEG; detail evidence finds six oversized images and six without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, keep intrinsic dimensions, and supply srcset/sizes matched to the one- and two-column card widths.

findings.summary: Third-party analytics, fonts and advertising consume disproportionate resources.
findings.evidence: The homepage sends 223,220 third-party bytes, including a 160,795-byte analytics script; the detail DOM also embeds a third-party jads.co advertising iframe.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove non-essential third parties, defer analytics/ads until appropriate, self-host a subset font, and lazy-load below-fold embeds.

taskList.title: Fix semantic controls, focus, target sizing, headings, alt text and captions
Deploy security headers and privacy-respecting analytics/cookies
Correct Burmese language metadata and logical layout properties
Improve LCP and remove critical-path/unused analytics code
Add descriptions, canonicals, Open Graph and VideoObject metadata
Modernize responsive image delivery and third-party budgets
Progressively add component queries and guided transitions/navigation
